newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -JGB tumult puts focus on puts, vols firm.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -JGB tumult puts focus on puts, vols firm.

text.p: A tumble in the Japanese government bond market on Thursday sparked interest in JGB puts, although dealers said that with volatility at high levels it could be a good time to sell vols.

Overnight, Japanese Ministry of Finance official Eisuke Sakakibara, known in financial markets as "Mr Yen", was quoted in a newspaper as saying the dollar's recovery was about to end, and that the MOF was not trying to push the yen down further.
The dollar lurched lower against the yen and both JGBs and U.S. Treasuries fell sharply after the remarks.
"A lot of people were already interested in put options in JGBs before this came out," said one London dealer.
He said flows did not look any heavier than usual but that there was a marked interest in the put side, if only for the reason that the market looked so toppy.
"When you get these kind of heavy highs, then it does prompt you to start looking at put options," the dealer said.
JGB futures have made successive high over the past four months, reaching a peak at 126.52 contract high in Tokyo on Wednesday.
"JGBs are a good example. Since the first quarter it hasn't really been doing anything on the downside," he said.
Alex McGuire, options trader at Sumitomo Finance International in London, said JGB over-the-counter vols had been rising over the past week.
He said three-month price volatilility on 10-year JGBs was at 5.2 percent, up from 4.4 at the end of October.
March JGB futures vols have risen to 6.2 from around five percent, he said.
"The market has been more volatile over the last week or two but not enough to justify these levels," he said. "I would be a seller rather than a buyer at the moment."

December JGB futures finished on LIFFE at 124.66, down from 124.75 at the Tokyo finish and down 1.11 from the prior LIFFE close. LIFFE March JGB were at 123.86, down one full point from the prior close.
